title: Instruction Magnetism — prompt curation & neutralization notes
content:
Quick concept note + running lab for an odd but recurring phenomenon: instruction magnetism.

Goal
- Capture a working definition and lightweight experiment matrix to (a) surface when prompts are being 'magnetized' by anchor examples and (b) try candidate neutralization strategies.
- Produce a small set of resilient templates we can hand to front-line SDK examples / docs.

Definition (working)
- Instruction magnetism: when particular instruction phrasing or example structures in a prompt disproportionately pull model outputs toward a repeated pattern, even if that pattern is irrelevant to the user's intent. Manifestations: semantic drift, repeated stylistic quirks, hallucinated constraints, and brittle error modes across different tasks.

Why I care (practical)
- Causes regression in real apps when a canned few-shot template over-constrains answers (e.g., always produce bulleted lists, always apologize).
- Hard to notice in unit tests: pass local eval but fail in production when user input distribution is different.

High-level hypotheses
H1: Magnetism scales with exemplar similarity + salience. If the few-shot exemplars are highly uniform (same label style, same tokens), they bias the next completion.
H2: Magnetism can be mitigated by contrastive exemplars (explicit negative examples) or by token-level neutralizers (prefixes that lower anchor salience).
H3: Temperature / sampling schedule interacts with magnetism: lower temp increases anchor pull.

Known failure modes (observed)
- Style lock: 'Always respond in a concise three-bullet list' persists even when user asks for a narrative.
- Constraint hallucination: model invents a constraint from the exemplar ("only use facts above") and refuses to add new info.
- Example overfitting: model repeats phrasings/idioms from the few shots verbatim.
- Instruction echo: prepended system messages meant to be invisible leak into responses.

Experiment matrix (minimal)
- Variables: exemplar uniformity (low / medium / high), exemplar polarity (all-positive / mixed / negative-negative examples), neutralizer type (empty / soft prefix / explicit breaker), temperature (0.0 / 0.4 / 0.8), model family (open-llama-70b / gpt-compatible-16k).
- Metrics: style divergence (Jensen-Shannon on bigram distributions vs. reference), factual willingness (binary: adds new info when asked), user-intent fidelity (pairwise human eval), repeat-token ratio (n-gram overlap with shots).

Concrete prompt templates to try (examples)
1) Baseline few-shot (magnetizable):
System: "You are a helpful assistant."
Shots: 3 Q/A showing the same bullet-list output format for each answer.
User: "Summarize the following article: ..."

2) Contrastive few-shot (mix polarity):
System: same
Shots: 2 examples where A produces bullets, 1 example where A produces a short paragraph labeled as "preferred alternate".

3) Negative exemplar inline (explicit anti-pattern):
System: "Do NOT follow the following example styles: '\n   - BAD: answer only in bullet fragments and ignore follow-ups'\n"
Shots: 2 neutral examples.

4) Soft neutralizer prefix (token-level):
System: "Ignore accidental stylistic cues in examples. Focus on intent: if user asks for narrative, produce narrative. If user asks for bullets, produce bullets."

5) Breaker separator (visual token injection):
Insert a long separator and a short meta-instruction after the shots: "---END EXAMPLES--- Next, answer the user's query."

Few-shot set design notes
- Vary lexicon: diversify function words across shots to reduce repeated n-grams.
- Avoid unusual punctuation patterns in exemplars (e.g., triple-dash lists) that models latch onto.
- Use explicit labels (EXAMPLE 1 / EXAMPLE 2) rather than natural conversation turns to reduce illusion of constraint.

Preliminary observations (local quick runs)
- Low-temp runs (0.0) strongly regressed to exemplar formatting; even when user asked for a different output type, the model persisted.
- Adding a single contrasting example reduced style-lock by ~30% (by JS divergence) on toy summaries.
- Negative exemplar phrasing ("BAD: ...") helped in some runs but occasionally produced a defensive tone in output (model repeated the negative phrasing). So negative examples work but can pollute style.
- Long separator + explicit meta-instruction sometimes reduces magnetism but increases verboseness (model interprets separator as heavy signal to 'start fresh' and then overexplains).

Evaluation rubric (quick)
- Fidelity to intent (0-3): Does output follow the user's requested format?
- Over-anchor score (0-3): How much of the answer is lexically identical to examples?
- Hallucination aggression (0-3): Does the model invent constraints or facts from examples?
- Style toxicity (0-3): Any odd phrasing introduced by negative exemplars or neutralizers.

Open questions / hypotheses to run next
- Can we build an automatic 'anchor salience' detector from attention proxies (token overlap / next-token bias estimates)?
- Is there a small set of neutralizer templates that generalize across tasks (summarization, classification, instruction-following)?
- Do shorter separators work better than very long ones? There may be a U-curve.

Short checklist for creating less-magnetizable few-shot sets (practical)
- diversify function words and punctuation across examples
- include at least one contrasting example that breaks the dominant pattern
- prefer explicit labels vs conversational glue
- avoid extreme formatting quirks in examples (emoji, ASCII art)
- test at multiple temperatures (0.0 and 0.4 at minimum)

Notes to self / TODOs
- Run 300-ex sample across the 5 templates above on the sandbox cluster (use model: open-llama-70b-quant). Compare metrics and push best neutralizer to docs. (Ethan for infra run)
- Create small human eval on MTurk or internal raters for fidelity/over-anchor. (Leila to draft HIT)
- Prototype an automatic 'style divergence' signal that can be surfaced as a debug metric in Console.
- Save failing cases to: linked_artifacts above + folder (will add after infra run).

Rough logs (scratch)
- 2024-11-07: first spot check — baseline few-shot produced identical sentence-level leads in 47% of cases.
- 2024-12-02: contrastive shot reduced identical leads to 29% but increased average length by 12 tokens.
- 2025-01-14: negative-exemplar trial created 2/50 outputs that echoed 'BAD:' wording. Need phrasing rehab.

Reference thoughts for docs/examples
- When shipping sample prompts in SDK/docs we should: 1) warn about anchor risk, 2) show both 'fragile' and 'robust' variants, 3) include a short checklist.

Weird micro-find: some models seem to treat list bullets ("- ") as a stronger anchor than full sentences. Might be useful to avoid leading with list syntax in example blasts.

End notes: this doc is intentionally messy — running log + hypotheses. Will refine into a short 'prompt hygiene' one-pager when we've got stable mitigations.

--Priya
